review: v3.3.1 post-Claude corpus and performance evidence
method: All artifact scans use --force --jobs 1 --level full and fresh SQLite outputs. Quality comparisons are non-timed. Real-corpus timing uses one unmeasured warm scan and five quiet-machine wall-clock samples. The adversarial scaling comparison uses one warm scan and three interleaved samples per binary.

diagnostic_set_comparison.plasma_cpp: Q_DECL_EXPORT diagnostic at kioworkers/desktop/kio_desktop.cpp:33 removed; Q_ASSERT error at applets/systemtray/systemtraymodel.cpp:94 retains the same kind and start span with only its end span extended. No new diagnostic failure was introduced.
diagnostic_set_comparison.qml: Kirigami and Quickshell diagnostic span sets exactly match v3.3.0.

declaration_family_checks.result: No v3.3.1 parse diagnostic occurs at sampled source sites; C++ focused macro suite also covers the restored declaration family.

wall_clock_samples_seconds.comparison: v3.3.1 p95 is higher on all four corpora: Plasma C++ 7.62 to 8.68 seconds (13.9%, non-overlapping samples), Kirigami C++ 0.77 to 0.88 seconds (14.3%, non-overlapping), Kirigami QML 1.22 to 1.25 seconds, and Quickshell QML 0.17 to 0.18 seconds. The aggregate scans do not isolate a causal repair.

adversarial_qt_macro_scaling.input: 169KB single-line C++ class containing Q_OBJECT and 10,000 members
adversarial_qt_macro_scaling.result: 40.8% lower v3.3.1 p95; the measured fix uses the precomputed line-start index instead of rescanning from byte zero per identifier.

limitations: No Windows corpus or timing verification was run.
The quality and wall-time runs exercise julie-extract directly; code-kb was used for source inspection but was not executed as a corpus workload.
Wall time includes process startup, parsing, extraction, and SQLite artifact creation; it does not prove the cause of any small runtime difference.
Third-party source remains untracked under target/qt-release-review and is not redistributed.
